newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini says EMU delay "useful" - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini says EMU delay "useful" - paper.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore that most EU countries were struggling to meet the criteria for European monetary and economic union (EMU) and that a delay would be useful.

"I believe that...a 12 month delay would be useful for everyone," Dini was quoted as saying in an interview published on Tuesday. The planned single European currency is due to be launched at the start of 1999.
The former Italian prime minister warned that EMU should not become a club for a privileged few states.

"We shouldn't forget that the euro can't go ahead without the necessary votes. Therefore the exclusion of Mediterranean countries together with, for example, Great Britain, could prevent the launch of EMU thanks to their negative votes," he was quoted as saying.
EMU founder members are due to be selected in early 1998 and Dini said he was convinced Italy would make the grade.
"Italy is very close to reaching the EMU criteria. I don't believe there will be any delays on our part," he said. "We're making the greatest effort."
